questions.text:
Let G be a graph with n vertices and m edges. What is the tightest upper bound on the
running time of Depth First Search on G, when G is represented as an adjacency matrix?
questions.solution:
With an adjacency matrix, finding the neighbours of a vertex means scanning its whole row of n entries. DFS does this for every vertex: [latex]n\times n=\Theta(n^2)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider rooted n node binary tree represented using pointers. The best upper bound on the
time required to determine the number of sub trees having exactly 4 nodes is [latex]O(n^{a}lob^{b}n)[/latex] .
Then the value of a+10b is_______
questions.solution:
A post-order traversal computes the size of every subtree (1 + left size + right size) in [latex]O(n)[/latex] total, and counts subtrees of size 4 along the way.

[latex]O(n)=O(n^1\log^0 n)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 1, b = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a + 10b = 1

Answer: 1

questions.text:
Consider the directed graph given below.

Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Edges: P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q, P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R, R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q, S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R, S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q. P and S have no incoming edges and can come first in either order; R must come before Q.

PSRQ and SPRQ are both valid; PQRS is not (Q before R).

Answer: Both PSRQ and SPRQ are topological orderings

options: The graph does not have any topological ordering
Both PQRS and SRQP are topological orderings
Both PSRQ and SPRQ are topological orderings.
PSRQ is the only topological ordering

questions.text:
Let P be a quick sort program to sort numbers in ascending order using the first element as
the pivot. Let t1 and t2 be the number of comparisons made by P for the inputs [1 2 3 4
5] and [4 1 5 3 2] respectively. Which one of the following holds?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [1 2 3 4 5] (sorted): every partition is maximally unbalanced: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 comparisons.
- [4 1 5 3 2]: pivot 4 (4 comparisons) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [2 1 3] and [5]; pivot 2 (2 comparisons) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [1] and [3]. Total 6.

[latex]t_1=10 \gt t_2=6[/latex]

Answer: [latex]t_1 \gt t_2[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Counting b's modulo 3 needs only 3 states, so "number of b's is 3k + 1" is regular. [latex]a^nb^n[/latex], prime-length strings and ww all need unbounded memory, so they are not regular.

Answer: The language with 3k+1 b's is regular

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The language L = {[latex]a^{n}[/latex]| n is prime} is regular
The language L={ w | w has 3k +1    b's for some k [latex]\in[/latex] N with [latex]\Sigma[/latex] = {a,b} } is regular.
The language L = { ww| w[latex]\in \Sigma^{*}[/latex] with [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={0,1}} is regular.
